commands.description: Decode Base64 encoded PowerShell command (Unicode).
Decompress and decode GZip-compressed Base64 payload.
commands.command:
$b64 = '<PASTE_BASE64_HERE>'
$bytes = [System.Convert]::FromBase64String($b64)
$ms = New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream(,$bytes)
$gz = New-Object System.IO.Compression.GZipStream($ms,[System.IO.Compression.CompressionMode]::Decompress)
$sr = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($gz)
$decompressed = $sr.ReadToEnd()
Write-Output '[+] Decompressed payload:'
Write-Output $decompressed

commands.description: Expand char-array obfuscation to readable string.
commands.command:
# Example: [char]73+[char]69+[char]88 -> IEX
$charArray = @(73,69,88)  # Replace with actual values
$result = -join ($charArray | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ })
Write-Output "[+] Decoded string: $result"

commands.description: Evaluate -replace chain obfuscation without executing payload.
commands.command:
# Safe static analysis of -replace obfuscation
$obfuscated = '<PASTE_OBFUSCATED_STRING>'
# Apply the replace chain statically to reveal original string
$result = $obfuscated -replace 'X','I' -replace 'Y','E' -replace 'Z','X'  # Adjust pairs
Write-Output "[+] After replace chain: $result"

hunt_account_lifecycle_anomalies.description: Hunt for account deletions, privilege flag changes, delegation abuse, service installation, and Task Scheduler persistence — covering Event IDs 4697, 4700, 4726, 4738, 5156, 6005, and TaskScheduler/Operational 106/141/200.

commands.description: Hunt for user account deletions — post-exploitation account cleanup (Event 4726).
commands.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4726} | Select TimeCreated,@{N='Actor';E={($_.Message -split 'Subject:\s+Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},@{N='DeletedAccount';E={($_.Message -split 'Target Account:\s+Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}} | Format-Table -AutoSize

commands.description: Hunt for user account changes enabling Kerberos delegation (TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION / DONT_REQ_PREAUTH) — Event 4738.
commands.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4738} | Where-Object { $_.Message -match '(TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION|DONT_REQ_PREAUTH|TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION|PASSWORD_NOT_REQUIRED)' } | Select TimeCreated,@{N='Actor';E={($_.Message -split 'Subject:\s+Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},@{N='Target';E={($_.Message -split 'Target Account:\s+Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},Message

commands.description: Hunt for services installed via Security log — attributes actor account unlike System Event 7045 (Event 4697).
commands.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4697} | Where-Object { $_.Message -notmatch '(System32|SysWOW64|Program Files|MsMpEng|WinDefend)' } | Select TimeCreated,@{N='Actor';E={($_.Message -split 'Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},@{N='ServiceName';E={($_.Message -split 'Service Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},@{N='ServiceFile';E={($_.Message -split 'Service File Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}} | Format-Table -AutoSize

commands.description: Hunt for dormant scheduled task enabled — pre-planted task activated (Event 4700).
commands.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4700} | Where-Object { $_.Message -notmatch '(SYSTEM|LOCAL SERVICE|NETWORK SERVICE)' } | Select TimeCreated,@{N='Actor';E={($_.Message -split 'Account Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}},@{N='Task';E={($_.Message -split 'Task Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()}}

commands.description: Hunt Task Scheduler operational log for task registrations, deletions, and executions (Events 106/141/200/201).
Hunt for WFP inbound connections to non-standard processes — C2 listener or reverse shell bind (Event 5156).
commands.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=5156} | Where-Object { $_.Message -match 'Direction:\s+%%14593' -and $_.Message -notmatch '(svchost|lsass|System|MsMpEng|SearchIndexer|dns|svchost)' } | Group-Object {($_.Message -split 'Application Name:\s+')[1].Split([char]10)[0].Trim()} | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select -First 10 Name,Count

commands.command:
